..
Issued at 130 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Currently surface observations and satellite depict low clouds, fog, 
and intermittent drizzle over the eastern U.P. this morning. In this 
post-frontal environment, cooler air over the moist maritime Great 
Lakes airmass has been contributing to the patchy fog and low 
stratus. This airmass will continue towards northern lower, brining 
low clouds, patchy fog, and off and on drizzle to some spots through 
sunrise. 24 hour rainfall totals show a handful of an inch or 
greater swaths, focused in NE lower and eastern upper. Other places 
saw a couple hundredths to a half of an inch. 

In the upper levels, an upper shortwave is exiting to the east this 
morning, with drier mid-level air gradually moving in behind this. A 
larger scale PNA pattern over the CONUS exists today, with upper 
ridging reaching into the NW Territory. The broad upper low over the 
Hudson Bay remains anchored in place, keeping MI locked in NW flow 
aloft. As this drier mid level air continues to march through 
northern MI today, the weak moisture boundary will reside over NE 
lower during peak diurnal heating. A few afternoon showers with a 
storm or two will be possible, as around a couple hundred j/kg of 
instability exists. NW lower will face drying air and shallow 
instability, keeping better chances closer to the sunrise side. 
Minimal shear exists in this marginally unstable atmosphere, keeping 
the main hazards brief heavy rain and lightning. Storms are expected 
to form right along an area of lower level convergence as the 
boundary reaches the lake shore (convergence set up is due to winds 
over the waters). This could keep most activity off shore, over Lk 
Huron. 

Friday, surface high pressure will be overhead. Light winds and 
times of sunshine will be seen over northern MI. A couple of 
stronger storm systems near the Pac NW will attempt to beat the 
upper ridge over the west down. This in turn, will create a southern 
extent of the upper jet over the central Rockies, which will produce 
lee cyclogenesis near CO. Hot and humid central plains air will push 
northward in the warm sector towards WI Friday. Warmer and wetter 
conditions will reach northern MI this weekend, with light rain 
chances starting as early as Saturday evening for eastern upper and 
parts of NW lower. Warmer temperatures, clouds, light rain, and 
embedded showers/storms will continue through early next week as the 
upper level trough takes it time moving across the northern rockies 
(inducing a couple of lee side lows during this time).

Global ensembles show this pattern in the QPF footprints. Most 
(ENS/GEFS and their AI counter parts) of them do highlight a 
bullseye of mean total QPF at 1" or more over northern MI by 
Wednesday of next week. These courser models will have a tough time 
with amounts, but can capture where the moisture and forcing will 
be. There is more of a spread in timing of when the deeper moisture 
reaches northern MI, as some hold off until Sunday. However by 
Sunday afternoon, 82% of LREF members have PWATs of at least 1.4" 
over KGLR. The high confidence in deeper moisture remains through 
early Tuesday morning, then PWAT spread increases Tuesday into 
midweek. 

Conceptually, the set up has the potential to orient the 
jet stream parallel to a few warm frontal boundaries that reach 
northern MI. This could result in training of storms producing heavy 
rainfall, which would lead to flooding. This is very dependent on 
the path of surface cyclones, and the warm front has been known to 
stall just to the south producing ideal conditions for convective 
initiation, which "eats" the moisture before it has time to reach 
northern MI. Guidance is pointing towards the synoptic scale forcing 
to be present to lift these features pretty far north, but that 
could change as we get closer to the event. 

Worse case is repeated rounds of training thunderstorms starting 
late Saturday and lasting through Tuesday, producing swaths of 2 to 
4 inches or more and resulting in flooding. With this said, this 
worse case is not favored (LREF probs of total QPF are only at 25% 
for 2 inches or more by Wednesday across parts of norther MI). The 
when and exactly where of this rain will determine impacts, and that 
can still change as we remain 4 to 5 days out.
